polarisation.label: Polarisation
polarisation.blurb: Two camps harden, neutral share collapses

mobilisation.label: Mobilisation
mobilisation.blurb: Calls to organise, escalate or act

traffic.note: Anger plus rising volume behaves very differently from fear plus rising volume. This one escalates rather than disperses.

water.note: Fear preceded anger here, which is the panic-buying signature rather than the protest signature.

exam.note: Still alarm, not anger. A correction published now lands; forty minutes later it argues with anger instead.

nep.note: The neutral share is the number to watch. Once it falls below roughly 15% the conversation stops being persuadable.

metro.note: The only tracked topic on the positive ladder. Advocacy decays back to approval rather than escalating.

lang.note: Polarisation preceded anger, so both camps are now mobilising. Counter-messaging into either one tends to harden the other.

power.note: This one is decaying, not escalating. Anger gave way to fatigue, which is why the crisis score sits well below the sentiment score.

flood.note: Alarm with trust still at 44 means official messaging is being believed. That window is the whole opportunity.

health.note: Slow-moving and fear-led. Misinformation risk is the live problem here, not velocity.
